dervis-irab:1-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ) التطفيف: short-changing in measure and weight, because what is withheld is something slight (طفيف) and paltry. طفف المكيال: he diminished the measure slightly. Al-Zajjāj said: "The one who diminishes the measure and the balance was called مطفف only because he hardly steals from the measure and the balance anything but a small, slight amount."
(اكْتالُوا) Al-Farrāʾ said: one says اكتلت على الناس: I took full measure from them; and اكتلت منهم: I took what was due from them; so على has the meaning of من.
(سِجِّينٍ) Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: Allah has reported of the record of the wicked that it is in سجين, and has explained سجين as a written record, so it is as though it were said: their record is in a written record — what does that mean? I say: سجين is a comprehensive book; it is the register of evil, in which Allah has recorded the deeds of the devils and the deeds of the disbelievers and the corrupt among jinn and humans. It is a written record, inscribed and clearly written, or marked, so that whoever sees it knows there is no good in it. So the meaning is that what is written of the deeds of the wicked is established in that register. It was named سجين, a faʿīl from السجن, which is imprisonment and constriction, because it is a cause of imprisonment and constriction in Hell," until he says: "If you say: what is سجين — is it an adjective or a noun? I say: rather, it is a proper noun transferred from an adjective, like حاتم, and it is triptote, because there is only one cause [of diptosis] in it, namely definiteness."
Abū Ḥayyān's wording: "As for سجين, the majority said it is a fiʿʿīl from السجن, like سكير; or in place of ساجن, so it came as an intensive form; on this view سجين is an adjective of an omitted place. Ibn Muqbil said:
ورفقة يضربون البيض ضاحية ... ضربا تواصت به الأبطال سجينا
(And a band of companions striking the helmets in broad daylight, with a lasting, severe blow which the heroes enjoined one another.)"
Then he cited what al-Zamakhsharī said, and said: "They differed over سجين, if it is a place, in a confused disagreement whose mention we have omitted. The apparent sense is that سجين is a book, and that is why كتاب مرقوم was made a badal (substitute) from it. ʿIkrima said: سجين is an expression for loss and abasement, as you say 'So-and-so has reached rock bottom' when he has become utterly inert. Some lexicographers said: the nūn of سجين is a substitute for a lām, and it is from السجل (the register). It is thus summarized from their statements that the nūn of سجين is either radical or a substitute for a lām; if it is radical, its derivation is from السجن."
The author of al-Qāmūs cited under the root سجن the following text: "And [سجين], like سكين: the lasting, the severe; a place in which is the record of the wicked; a valley in Hell — may Allah the Exalted protect us from it; or a rock in the seventh earth."
(مَرْقُومٌ) written, inscribed. The basic meaning of الرقم is writing; and from it is the poet's saying:
سأرقم في الماء القراح إليكم ... على بعدكم إن كان للماء راقم
(I shall write to you on clear water, despite your distance, if water has anyone who can write on it.)

* I'rab:
(وَيْلٌ لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ) (ويل) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); what licenses beginning with it is its being an imprecation; and (للمطففين) is its khabar (predicate). Had it been accusative, that would have been permissible. It has been said: "The preferred form for ويل and its like, when it is not in a genitive construct, is the nominative, and the accusative is permissible; if it is in a construct or made definite, the preferred form is the accusative, as in ويلكم لا تغترّوا."
(الَّذِينَ إِذَا اكْتالُوا عَلَى النَّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ) (الذين) is an adjective of (المطففين). (إذا) is an adverb for future time containing the meaning of condition, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its implied form being "they took from them". The clause (اكتالوا) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (على الناس) is attached to (اكتالوا); it has also been said that it is attached to (يستوفون), the object having been placed before the verb only to convey specificity. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Since their taking measure was a taking of measure that harmed [people] and in which they were imposed upon, على was substituted in place of من to indicate that. It may also be attached to يستوفون, the object being placed before the verb to convey specificity, i.e. they take full measure from people in particular; as for themselves, they take full measure for them." Ibn Hishām made «على» mean «من», agreeing in that with al-Zamakhsharī. The clause (يستوفون) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of the omitted apodosis, i.e. they took from them, taking full measure.
(وَإِذا كالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction. (إذا) is an adverb for future time attached to the omitted apodosis, its implied form being "they took full measure for it". The clause (كالوهم) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (كالوهم) is a past verb and its fāʿil, and the hāʾ [i.e. هم] is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. they measured the food out for them. (أو) is a conjunction, and (وزنوهم) is conjoined to (كالوهم) and parsed in parallel with it. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "The pronoun in كالوهم أو وزنوهم is an accusative pronoun referring to الناس, and there are two views on it: that what is meant is كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم, with the preposition omitted and the verb joined directly, as he said:
ولقد جنيتك أكمؤا وعساقلا ... ولقد نهيتك عن نبات الأوبر
(I gathered truffles and ʿasāqil for you, and I forbade you the daughters of Awbar.)"
جنى is transitive only to one object, and to the second by means of the lām; so the original is جنيت لك, with the preposition omitted and the pronoun joined directly; or it was made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of انجتك [Translator's note: so in the source; apparently a corruption of a verb such as أجنيتك or أنلتك] and so made transitive to both. الأكمؤ is the plural of كمء, like أفلس; it is the singular of الكمأة, which is a large kind of plant called "the fat of the earth"; it was called كمأة because of its being known by it. العساقل is the plural of عسقول, like عصفور; its due form was عساقيل, but the yāʾ was dropped for the metre. It has been said that it is the plural of عسقل, which is a small, good, white kind of it. بنات أوبر are a poor, black, downy kind of it, as though it had fur on it; it has been said that it is a species resembling colocasia or turnip. بنات أوبر is the plural of ابن أوبر, because it is a proper name for something non-rational, and the al in it is redundant (zāʾida). Al-Mubarrad said: it is a generic noun. The verse is of the type of allegory (tamthīl) for the state of one who was urged towards the good but turned aside to the bad, then came back regretting its outcome. We return to what we are about, and say: among examples of what is accusative by removal of the preposition is their saying الحريص يصيدك لا الجواد ("the eager one catches for you, not the steed"), the original being يصيد لك. What has been said, that هم is a nominative pronoun emphasizing the wāw in (كالوهم), is a mistake. (أو) is a conjunction, and (وزنوهم) is conjoined to (كالوهم); the same is said in its parsing as was said about (كالوهم), i.e. وزنوا لهم. Abū Ḥayyān's wording: "كال and وزن are among the verbs made transitive by a preposition; so you say كلت لك and وزنت لك, and the lām may be omitted, as in your saying نصحت لك and نصحتك, شكرت لك and شكرتك. The pronoun is an accusative pronoun, i.e. كالوا لهم ووزنوا لهم, with the preposition omitted and the verb joined by itself; and the object, which is what is measured or weighed, is omitted." The clause (يخسرون) is a ḥāl from the omitted apodosis.
(أَلا يَظُنُّ أُولئِكَ أَنَّهُمْ مَبْعُوثُونَ لِيَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ لِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval, (لا) is negative, and (يظن) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ). الظن here means certainty, i.e. are those not certain? Had they been certain, they would not have diminished the measure and the weight. (أولئك) is the fāʿil, the reference being to those who give short measure. (أنّ) with what is in its scope stands in place of the two objects of (يظن). (أنّ) and its noun; (مبعوثون) is its khabar; and (ليوم) is attached to (مبعوثون), or it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and it is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa only because of its annexation to the verb [Translator's note: this remark evidently refers to the alternative of (يوم يقوم) being in the nominative position yet ending in fatḥa; it is so placed in the source]. (عظيم) is a naʿt (adjective). (يوم) is a badal from (ليوم), following it in position; its position is accusative by the mentioned (مبعوثون) or by an implied verb like it, because the badal is on the intention of repeating the governor. The clause (يقوم الناس) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and (لرب العالمين) is attached to (يقوم). It is reported of Ibn ʿUmrān [Translator's note: so in the source; the report is known of Ibn ʿUmar] that he recited this sūra, and when he reached His saying يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين he wept aloud and was unable to recite what came after it. It is reported of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān that a Bedouin said to him: "You have heard what Allah said about those who give short measure" — by that he meant: the one who gives short measure has had this tremendous threat, which you have heard, directed at him; so what do you think of yourself, when you take the wealth of the Muslims without measure or weight?
(كَلَّا إِنَّ كِتابَ الفُجَّارِ لَفِي سِجِّينٍ وَما أَدْراكَ ما سِجِّينٌ كِتابٌ مَرْقُومٌ) (كلا) is a rebuke and restraint for them from giving short measure and from heedlessness of the Reckoning and the Resurrection. (إنّ) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and (في سجين) is the khabar of (إنّ). (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (أدراك) is the khabar. (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and (سجين) is the khabar; the nominal clause, suspended (muʿallaqa) by the interrogative, stands in place of the second object of (أدراك). (كتاب) is a badal from (سجين), or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is a written record"; and (مرقوم) is an adjective of (كتاب). If (سجين) is considered the name of a place, then the khabar reading is preferable, or one assumes an annexed noun omitted before (سجين), so as to ward off the objection: سجين is the name of a place, so how can it be explained as a written record?
(وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ الَّذِينَ يُكَذِّبُونَ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ) (ويل) is a mubtadaʾ, as has preceded; (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to (ويل); (للمكذبين) is the khabar; (الذين) is a naʿt of (المكذبين); the clause (يكذبون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين); and (بيوم الدين) is attached to (يكذبون).
(وَما يُكَذِّبُ بِهِ إِلَّا كُلُّ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ) The wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (ما) is negative; (يكذب) is an imperfect verb in the nominative; (به) is attached to (يكذب); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (كل معتد أثيم) is the fāʿil of (يكذب).
(إِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِ آياتُنا قالَ أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ) (إذا) is a future adverb containing the meaning of condition, attached to its apodosis, which is (قال). The clause (تتلى) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; (عليه) is attached to (تتلى); and (آياتنا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (تتلى). The clause (قال) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of (إذا). (أساطير الأولين) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. هي. It has preceded that الأساطير is the plural of أسطورة or أساطرة [Translator's note: so in the source; usually given as إسطارة], with kasra, which is a tale written down long ago.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون» there is antithesis (muqābala), which came in the finest and most orderly way: i.e. when the measuring is on the part of others, they take it in full, and when the measuring is on their own part in particular, they make it deficient, whether they carry it out themselves or not. The pronoun does not indicate carrying out personally, nor does it hint at that. What shows you that the pronoun does not convey carrying out the act personally is that you may say: "The rulers are the ones who carry out the prescribed punishments, not the common people," and you do not mean that they carry it out themselves; its meaning is only that doing that is on their part in particular. It has been said that the people of Medina were merchants who gave short measure, and their sales were al-munābadha [Translator's note: the source prints المنابزة, for المنابذة], al-mulāmasa and al-mukhāṭara (forms of gambling sales). So it was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and recited it to them and said: "Five for five." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is five for five?" He said: "No people break the covenant but Allah sets their enemy over them; they do not judge by other than what Allah has revealed but poverty spreads among them; indecency does not appear among them but death spreads among them; they do not give short measure but they are denied vegetation and seized with years of famine; and they do not withhold the zakāt but rain is held back from them." It has also been said that it was revealed about a man known as Abū Juhayna who had two ṣāʿ-measures: he measured out with one and took measure with the other, i.e. he took with one and gave with the other.
